scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: Orders with 2 captures were 0 on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08, then 118 on 09-09 and 124 on 09-10, equal to gateway timeout retries on those days.

F-02.statement: CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY set idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off (temporary, latency debugging); rollback was not executed.

F-03.statement: Double-charge tickets were 9 (W35) and 11 (W36), then 288 (W37) and 301 (W38), on about 21,000 orders per week.

F-04.statement: On 2026-09-09..10, all 242 duplicate orders came from gateway-timeout retries sent without an idempotency key. On 09-01..08, 238 retries carried keys and the PSP deduplicated all of them.

F-05.statement: Per payments change runbook section 4, set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after SH-OPS confirms it at runtime; the change is reversible.

F-06.statement: The charge ledger shows 4 orders with 2 captures that are not refunded: O-90211 (54.0), O-90244 (19.9), O-90302 (120.0), O-90318 (33.5).

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-APOLOGY-REPLY-GAP.statement: The core problem is that customer service lacks efficient, well-worded replies to double-charge complaints, so an apology-drafting assistant addresses it.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: Idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries was disabled by a gateway configuration change, so retries create duplicate captures.

H-RETRY-LOGIC-DEFECT.statement: A defect in the shop's checkout or capture retry logic, such as timeouts causing retries with new idempotency keys, creates duplicate captures without any config change.

H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATION.statement: The PSP processes or logs a single capture request twice, so duplication originates on the PSP side of the capture handoff.

H-PERCEIVED-DUPLICATE-AUTH-HOL.statement: Many complaints reflect a pending authorization plus a final capture that customers see as two charges, not actual duplicate captures.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Duplicate captures are real and began on 2026-09-09. From then, every gateway-timeout retry produced a second capture, while retry volume stayed flat at about 120 a day.

CHG-77 by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 turned idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off, noted as temporary for latency debugging, and was not rolled back. The date matches the onset of duplicate captures in E-01.

Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week (W35, W36) to 288 and 301 (W37, W38) on roughly flat order volume. The step change fits the 2026-09-09 onset of duplicate captures, so most complaints look like real duplicates.

PSP logs show all 242 duplicate orders on 09-09..10 came from gateway-timeout retries sent without idempotency keys. From 09-01..08, 238 keyed retries were all deduplicated by the PSP, so the cause is on the shop side, not the PSP.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments engineer states he disabled idempotency-key enforcement on 09-09 for latency debugging, and that timeout and retry rates are unchanged, so the keyless retries now create duplicates. This is a stakeholder claim that agrees with E-02 and E-04. He also says re-enabling is a one-setting change that payments operations must confirm at runtime.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook (E-07) says automation may run set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and that the change is reversible. It is a procedural authorization document, not causal evidence, so it bears on how the fix may be executed and not on why duplicates occur.

A-REENABLE-FIXES.statement: Re-enabling enforcement stops new duplicates, as it did before 09-09 when all 238 keyed retries were deduplicated.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers complaining about double charges (CL-01); not adopted as the problem definition.
symptoms: Orders with 2 captures went from 0 (09-07, 09-08) to 118 and 124 (09-09, 09-10) (E-01)
Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week to 288 and 301 per week (E-03)
All 242 duplicate orders on 09-09..10 were keyless timeout retries (E-04)
problem_definition.root_problem: Since 2026-09-09, orders are charged twice because CHG-77 turned idempotency-key enforcement off, so gateway-timeout retries reach the PSP without keys and are captured a second time (E-01, E-02, E-04). The resulting real duplicates explain the jump in double-charge tickets (E-03).

structural_remedies.description: Re-enable idempotency-key enforcement via set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config, which rolls back CHG-77. Run it only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime.
structural_remedies.rationale: It is a one-setting reversible change (E-05, E-07). Authorization DA-SET-CAPTURE-IDEMPOTENCY is granted to SH-OPS, and K-GW requires runtime confirmation by SH-OPS. 225 minutes remain.; residual gap: Customers already double-charged are not fixed (U-EXISTING-DUPS). The latency reason for CHG-77 is unresolved (U-LATENCY-REASON). Success needs validation per SC-1 and SC-2.

structural_remedies.description: Add a process rule that temporary gateway config changes carry an expiry or rollback owner. Alert when idempotency enforcement is off.
structural_remedies.rationale: It is a process and config-monitoring change. It prevents recurrence but does not stop the current duplicates, and it is not needed to meet the success criteria.; residual gap: It does not stop the ongoing duplicates or refund affected customers. It needs an owner (SH-OPS or SH-PAY) after the immediate fix.

structural_remedies.description: Have payments operations identify unrefunded duplicate captures from the charge ledger (DA-CHG) and refund them under the existing refund process.
structural_remedies.rationale: The ledger is readable (payments-db HEALTHY). A refund is a separate process outside the tool surface, so it is a human or ops step. VOB-U-EXISTING-DUPS must be resolved before release.; residual gap: It addresses existing harm only. It does not prevent new duplicates unless remedy reenable_idempotency is also done.

proposal.summary: The problem was defined as real duplicate charges since 2026-09-09, caused by CHG-77 turning idempotency-key enforcement off, so keyless gateway-timeout retries were captured twice (E-01, E-02, E-04). This also explains the jump in double-charge tickets (E-03). The requested apology-reply assistant (CL-01) was not adopted, because its hypothesis was rejected (H-APOLOGY-REPLY-GAP). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the release scope is a proposal to re-enable enforcement plus monitoring of captures and tickets. The decision is not a hold because the open items are non-critical or tracked, and the DEFINE gate was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS. Nothing has been changed yet; re-enabling needs runtime confirmation by SH-OPS (E-07).
key_points: Duplicate captures were 0 on 09-07 and 09-08, then 118 and 124 on 09-09 and 09-10, matching daily timeout retries, which stayed flat at about 120 (E-01).
The config audit shows CHG-77 by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 set idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off as temporary, and it was not rolled back (E-02).
PSP logs show all 242 duplicate orders on 09-09..10 were keyless timeout retries. From 09-01..08, all 238 keyed retries were deduplicated, so the cause is on the shop side (E-04).
Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week to 288 and 301 per week on flat order volume (E-03). The SH-PAY interview agrees with the records (E-05), but it is only a stakeholder claim.
The PSP-side, retry-logic and pending-authorization explanations were rejected (H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATION, H-RETRY-LOGIC-DEFECT, H-PERCEIVED-DUPLICATE-AUTH-HOL). H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED was confirmed.

Released: a proposal to re-enable enforcement through set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config (SR-REENABLE-IDEMPOTENCY). It runs only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and the change is reversible (E-07). Also released: monitoring of duplicate captures (SC-1) and weekly tickets (SC-2).
The ledger lists 4 unrefunded duplicate-capture orders: O-90211, O-90244, O-90302 and O-90318 (E-08). The refund remedy SR-REFUND-EXISTING-DUPS is feasible but is not part of the release scope.
limitations_explained: Customers already double-charged are not fixed by this release. Four unrefunded orders are identified (E-08), but refunds are a separate step for payments operations.
It is unresolved whether re-enabling enforcement brings back the capture latency that CHG-77 was meant to debug (U-LATENCY-REASON, VOB-R-2). This is non-critical but still open.

Recurrence is not prevented. The process rule that gives temporary gateway changes an expiry or rollback owner, with an alert when enforcement is off, is not feasible in contest time (SR-CHANGE-CONTROL-GUARD).
Whether capture requests are delivered to the PSP, and whether they are semantically valid, is unknown (H-CAPTURE). This is why the DEFINE gate was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS.

The fix is only a proposal until SH-OPS confirms at runtime. The gateway-config tool health is UNKNOWN, so the effect on new duplicates (SC-1) is not yet shown. That it stops them rests on an active assumption (A-REENABLE-FIXES).

Ticket recovery to about 11 per week (SC-2) may lag because of the weekly measurement window and existing duplicate victims. That most tickets are real duplicates also rests on an assumption (A-TICKET-REAL-DUPS).
